title: 2020年7月四级真题 第1套 阅读1
paperTitle: 2020年7月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
passage:
P1 The wallet is heading for extinction. As a day-to-day essential, it will die off with the generation who read print newspapers. The kind of shopping where you hand over notes and count out change in return now happens only in the most minor of our retail encounters, like buying a bar of chocolate or a pint of milk, from a corner shop. At the shops where you spend any real money, that money is increasingly abstracted. And this is more and more true, the higher up the scale you go. At the most cutting-edge retail stores Victoria Beckham on Dover Street, for instance you don't go and stand at any kind of cash register, when you decide to pay. The staff are equipped with iPads to take your payment while you relax on a sofa.

P2 Which is nothing more or less than excellent service, if you have the money. But across society, the abstraction of the idea of cash makes me uneasy. Maybe I'm just old-fashioned. But earning money isn't quick or easy for most of us. Isn't it a bit weird that spending it should happen in half a blink(眨眼) of an eye? Doesn't a wallet—that time-honoured Friday-night feeling of pleasing, promising fatness— represent something that matters?

P3 But I'll leave the economics to the experts. What bothers me about the death of the wallet is the change it represents in our physical environment. Everything about the look and feel of a wallet—the way the fastenings and materials wear and tear and loosen with age, the plastic and paper and gold and silver, and handwritten phone numbers and printed cinema tickets—is the very opposite of what our world is becoming. The opposite of a wallet is a smartphone or an iPad. The rounded edges, cool glass, smooth and unknowable as a pebble(鹅卵石). Instead of digging through pieces of paper and peering into corners, we move our fingers left and right. No more counting out coins. Show your wallet, if you still have one. It may not be here much longer.

questions.q: What is happening to the wallet?
options: It is disappearing.
It is being fattened.
It is becoming costly.
It is changing in style.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What is happening to the wallet 是开放式 what 问句，直接问钱包“正在发生什 么”，不含 infer/suggest/imply，属于对原文事实的客观转述。

【拆句】Q46 主干 What is happening to the wallet，what 作主语，is happening 现在进行时， to the wallet 介宾短语作状语，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】The wallet is heading for extinction. As a day-to-day essential, it will die off with the generation who read print newspapers. 钱包正走向消亡。作为日常必需品，它将随着读纸质报纸的那代人一起消失。 46. What is happening to the wallet? A) It is disappearing. B) It is being fattened. C) It is becoming costly. D) It is changing in style.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 heading for extinction ↔disappearing 预判的“正在消失”与 disappearing 在词义、时态上完全吻合，无须再权衡其他选项。 B) 偷换概念 being fattened 把 fatness 这处比喻钱包鼓胀的怀旧描写当成了事实陈述——原文是 “过去周五发薪那种鼓胀的感觉令人愉悦”，并不是说钱包真的在变厚。 C) 无中生有 becoming costly 说“钱包变得昂贵”，全文从未讨论钱包本身的售价或制造成本，仅讨 论它的“消亡”与“象征意义”。 D) 与原文相反 changing in style 暗示钱包还在、只是换了款式，与 heading for extinction 与 It may not be here much longer 表达的“将不复存在”相反。 大型现代商店里的商业交易是如何完成的? A) 单独进行。 B) 通过电子方式。 C) 以抽象的方式。 D) 通过收银机。

questions.q: How are business transactions done in big modern stores?
options: Individually.
Electronically.
In the abstract.
Via cash register.
questions.explain:
【判型】How are business transactions done 用 how 直问交易在大店里怎么完成，要的是原文对 做法的客观描述。

【拆句】Q47 主干 transactions are done，被动语态，how 问做法的方式，介词短语 in big modern stores 限定场景。

【定位】At the most cutting-edge retail stores—Victoria Beckham on Dover Street, for instance—you don't go and stand at any kind of cash register, when you decide to pay. The staff are equipped with iPads to take your payment while you relax on a sofa. 在最前沿的零售店里——比如多佛街上的维多利亚·贝克汉姆店——付款时你根本不用去站 在任何收银台前。店员配备了 iPad，你舒服地坐在沙发上，他们就给你结账。 47. How are business transactions done in big modern stores? A) Individually. B) Electronically. C) In the abstract. D) Via cash register.

【选项】A) 过度推断 Individually 意为“一对一/单独地”，原文虽提到坐在沙发上接受服务的舒适感，但并未 把这种服务方式称为 individually，也未与“群体性服务”对比。 B) ✓ 正确 The staff are equipped with iPads to take your payment ↔Electronically 预判“用电子设备付款”恰好被 Electronically 这一上位副词完整覆盖，定位与替换两端 都通。 C) 答非所问 In the abstract 取自 the abstraction of the idea of cash，那是作者对现象的评价 （金钱概念被抽象化），并非交易“如何完成”的具体做法。 D) 与原文相反 Via cash register 说“通过收银台”，但定位句明说 you don't go and stand at any kind of cash register——大店里恰恰不用收银台。 是什么让作者在当今感到不舒服? A) 省钱正在成为过去的事情。 B) 令人愉快的周五晚上的感觉正在消退。 C) 挣钱正变得更加困难。 D) 花钱如此快速和容易。

questions.q: What makes the author feel uncomfortable nowadays?
options: Saving money is becoming a thing of the past.
The pleasing Friday-night feeling is fading.
Earning money is getting more difficult.
Spending money is so fast and easy.
questions.explain:
【判型】What makes the author feel uncomfortable 直问导致作者不适的事物，答案在原文中有 对应陈述，不需推断。

【拆句】Q48 主干 What makes the author feel uncomfortable，使役结构 make sb do，what 作主语问主语本身，nowadays 时间状语限定范围。

【定位】But across society, the abstraction of the idea of cash makes me uneasy. Maybe I'm just old- fashioned. But earning money isn't quick or easy for most of us. Isn't it a bit weird that spending it should happen in half a blink of an eye? 但放眼整个社会，金钱概念被抽象化这件事让我不安。也许我只是老派。但挣钱对大多数人 来说既不快也不轻松。花钱却能在眨眼之间完成，这难道不有点怪吗？ 48. What makes the author feel uncomfortable nowadays? A) Saving money is becoming a thing of the past. B) The pleasing Friday-night feeling is fading. C) Earning money is getting more difficult. D) Spending money is so fast and easy.

【选项】A) 无中生有 Saving money is becoming a thing of the past 说“存钱在变成过去式”，原文从未讨 论存钱（saving），只讨论花钱与挣钱。 B) 张冠李戴 The pleasing Friday-night feeling is fading 取自 that time-honoured Friday-night feeling of pleasing, promising fatness，但原文用这一感受作“钱包代表着重要的东西” 的论据，不是作者声称的不安根源；他不安的是 spending it should happen in half a blink of an eye。 C) 偷换概念 Earning money is getting more difficult 把原文 earning money isn't quick or easy for most of us 的“挣钱本来就不快不易”误读成“挣钱正变得更难”——原文没有“更难 （在变化中）”的意思，且作者不舒服的真正对象是花钱、不是挣钱。 D) ✓ 正确 spending it should happen in half a blink of an eye ↔Spending money is so fast and easy 预判“花钱太快太轻易”与 Spending money is so fast and easy 字面一一对应，不需要 权衡其他选项。 作者为什么选择写钱包正在发生的变化? A) 它代表了现代世界的一种变化。 B) 它与每个人的生活都有关系。 C) 它标志着一个历史悠久的传统的终结。 D) 它是当代经济学家关注的问题。

questions.q: Why does the author choose to write about what's happening to the wallet?
options: It represents a change in the modern world.
It has something to do with everybody's life.
It marks the end of a time-honoured tradition.
It is the concern of contemporary economists.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why does the author choose to write 问的是作者的写作动机，原文不会一字一句写“我 写本文是因为…”，需要从作者明确表达“在意什么”的句子做一步延伸。

【拆句】Q49 主干 Why does the author choose to write about X，choose to + 不定式作宾 语，about 引导写作话题，what's happening to the wallet 名词性从句作 about 的 宾语。

【定位】But I'll leave the economics to the experts. What bothers me about the death of the wallet is the change it represents in our physical environment. 但我把经济这层留给专家。真正困扰我的，是钱包消亡所代表的、我们身处的物理环境的 变化。 49. Why does the author choose to write about what's happening to the wallet? A) It represents a change in the modern world. B) It has something to do with everybody's life. C) It marks the end of a time-honoured tradition. D) It is the concern of contemporary economists.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 the change it represents in our physical environment ↔ represents a change in the modern world 预判“钱包代表着当代世界的某种变化”与 It represents a change in the modern world 完全对应。 B) 过度推断 has something to do with everybody's life 说钱包消失与“每个人的生活”都相关，原 文虽然提到 across society，但作者强调的是“我真正在意的是它代表的变化”，并不是 “它和每个人有关”。 C) 以偏概全 It marks the end of a time-honoured tradition 取自 that time-honoured Friday- night feeling，但 time-honoured 只是描述周五夜感受的形容词，全文并不是把钱包 写作“一种古老传统的终结”，而是借它说环境变化。 D) 与原文相反 concern of contemporary economists 说钱包消失是当代经济学家关心的事，但作者 在定位句开头就写明 I'll leave the economics to the experts，把经济视角主动让出去 ——这正是他写本文的动机所排除的对象。 从文章中我们可以推断出作者什么? A) 他抵制社会变革。 B) 他反对技术进步。 C) 他不愿放弃传统钱包。 D) 他在不断变化的现代世界中感到不安全。

questions.q: What can we infer from the passage about the author?
options: He is resistant to social changes.
He is against technological progress.
He feels reluctant to part with the traditional wallet.
He feels insecure in the ever-changing modern world.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What can we infer from the passage about the author 直接用 infer 提示推断题， 要求基于全文判断作者形象。

【拆句】Q50 主干 What can we infer，情态动词 can 表能力可能，from the passage 与 about the author 是两个并列介宾短语分别交代依据与对象，结构平稳无陷阱。 50. What can we infer from the passage about the author? A) He is resistant to social changes. B) He is against technological progress. C) He feels reluctant to part with the traditional wallet. D) He feels insecure in the ever-changing modern world.

【选项】A) 过度推断 resistant to social changes 说作者抗拒“社会变化”——但作者 Maybe I'm just old- fashioned 已自嘲只是老派，且 I'll leave the economics to the experts 表明他不打算 就更大范围的社会议题表态。 B) 与原文相反 against technological progress 说作者反对科技进步，但作者明确称 Which is nothing more or less than excellent service——他承认电子化是优秀服务；他不满的 是钱包消亡所代表的物理环境变化，而非科技本身。 C) ✓ 正确 Everything about the look and feel of a wallet—the way the fastenings and materials wear and tear and loosen with age, the plastic and paper and gold and silver, and handwritten phone numbers and printed cinema tickets—is the very opposite of what our world is becoming ↔reluctant to part with the traditional wallet Show your wallet, if you still have one. It may not be here much longer ↔ reluctant to part with the traditional wallet 三段表态聚合出“对传统钱包眷恋而不舍”，与 He feels reluctant to part with the traditional wallet 完全吻合。 D) 无中生有 feels insecure in the ever-changing modern world 说作者在“日新月异的现代世界感 到不安全”，原文里作者表达的是不安（uneasy）与困扰（bothers me），均针对钱包 消亡这一具体事，没有任何对“安全感缺失”的描述。
